_meta.description: Source of truth for all hosting plan pricing across the DronaHost website. Import this file in components, generateMetadata(), and JSON-LD schemas. Copy never contains a number or promise that is not rendered from this file or from content/claims.ts.
_meta.renewalPolicy: Renewal price equals the signup price for the same billing cycle. No introductory price that rises at renewal. Show the claim wording only when claim renewal-price-same renders.
_meta.annualSavings: Paying annually costs about 19% to 21% less per month than paying monthly in USD; other currencies differ by up to a point after rounding. The site works out the saving from each currency's own prices.
_meta.currencyNote: USD is the base. GBP, EUR, AED and INR prices were calculated once from fixed rates per 1 USD (currencies[].rateFromUSD: GBP 0.76, EUR 0.89, AED 3.6725, INR 96.8; market rates of 8 to 10 October 2026, owner choice 2026-10-12) and rounded up to the next .99 (INR: the next whole rupee). Each price is stored, never converted at runtime. Renewal equals the signup price in every currency. To change a currency's prices, change its rate and recalculate every plan and add-on, or edit the stored prices. Email plans (emailPlans) stay USD only.
_meta.emailNotice: Email is not included with any hosting plan. Email is a separate service, sold on its own.
changesFromV2: 4.1.0 (2026-10-12, owner): GBP, EUR, AED and INR prices for every plan and add-on, from fixed rates (GBP 0.76, EUR 0.89, AED 3.6725, INR 96.8 per USD) rounded up to .99 (INR to the whole rupee). Renewal equals signup in every currency. The currency selector is on. USD prices unchanged.

4.0.1 (2026-10-11, owner): corrections, no price or limit changed. Backups: only the latest daily copy is kept, so backupRetentionDays is 1 on every plan and the cards say 'Daily backup, latest copy kept'. Extra Layer Security is included on Pro and Scale and a paid add-on on Starter and Growth; its placeholder sentence is removed. Add-ons drop the removed Essential and Plus and add Scale. annualSavings corrected to 19% to 21%. null now means 'not set, render nothing'; fair-use limits are listed in limits.fairUse (Scale: sites, domains, databases, bandwidth), and limits.trafficType is removed. limits.trafficGB is removed: bandwidth lives only in internal.bandwidthGB. PHP limits come from the PHP settings tab. Headline features name what each higher plan adds. includedWithEveryPlan adds advanced security and server monitoring; the control panel item and its claim are renamed from 'cpanel' to 'control-panel'.

4.0.0 (2026-10-11, owner): one four-plan lineup from data/dronahost-pricing-plan.xlsx (Plans tab) replaces both families. Starter, Growth, Pro and Scale; Essential and Plus are removed. Prices, sites, NVMe storage, databases, backup days, bandwidth, support tier, performance tuning, Redis (Scale), resource type, CPU and RAM come from the sheet. Rule-safe handling (owner choice): 'Unlimited' is stored as null (fair use, never 'Unlimited'); mailboxes and bandwidth are internal only; visits per month are empty until load-tested; Imunify360 is stored as advancedSecurity and malwareScanning, not named; Redis is gated by a claim; the Growth badge is 'Recommended' (not 'Most popular'); Enterprise uses 'Talk to the team', not WhatsApp. PHP limits are carried over from the old plans (Scale copies Pro) because only the Plans tab was applied.

2026-10-11 (owner, final): staging with clone and sync in the control panel is available on every WordPress plan (corrects the earlier removal). Advanced security on every plan means three layers: a firewall, brute-force protection and malware scanning. Backups have two layers: local and offsite. Paid extras: premium SSL (not priced yet), extra offsite backup and Extra Layer Security. Earlier the same day: malware scanning, advanced security and a free domain for the first year (annual billing only) on every plan; WooCommerce optimization only on the Business hosting plans (Essential, Plus); NGINX caching and a daily backup with the latest copy kept on every WordPress plan. Redis object cache and automated plugin testing are not offered and are false on every plan (staging was briefly removed, then restored as above). Starter support is 24/7 like every plan. LiteSpeed is not used (removed from includedWithEveryPlan). The Automatic Malware Scanning add-on is removed because malware scanning is included on every plan; Extra Layer Security stays an add-on. WordPress hosting runs on Plesk.
Mailboxes removed from all limits. Email hosting is discontinued.

3.2.0 (2026-10-10): email is never part of a hosting plan or a hosting add-on. Email will be sold as a separate service with its own plans (owner decision 49). Business Email plans live in emailPlans, outside plans[], priced from Google Workspace US list prices (decision 54).
Scale, Dedicated Core and Enterprise moved out of the public plan list into highTraffic (talk to us).
Two Web hosting plans added: essential and plus.
Starter backup retention raised from 1 day to 7 days.
Disk sizes now follow the advisor tables (WordPress 20/60/120 GB, Web 15/50 GB), not the old file (200/500/1000 GB). Confirm which is real.
Site counts capped (Growth 10, Pro 25, Plus 10). No 'unlimited' wording.
Non-USD prices, regions block and first-response times removed.
Unverified performance multipliers removed from includedWithEveryPlan. Each included item now carries a claimId.
Offsite backup add-on collapsed into one add-on with size options.
3.1.0: support channels reduced to ticket and email. WhatsApp, live chat and phone are not offered (owner decision 22, 2026-10-07).
CTA labels follow the 'Choose {plan name}' rule. Badge 'Most Popular' replaced by 'Recommended'.
confirmBeforeLaunch: Support hours: the sheet gives Starter 'Standard' and Growth 'Priority' with no hours, while /support-policy promises 24/7 by ticket and email to everyone. Settle which is right (availability is empty for Starter and Growth).

Plan scope: these four plans now serve WordPress and Business pages alike. Confirm which managed WordPress tools (automatic updates, NGINX caching, staging) apply to every plan, and whether WooCommerce optimization is on any plan (false everywhere until confirmed).
Redis on Scale: decision 61 said Redis is not offered; claim it before any page mentions it.
Visits per month per plan, after a load test (sheet row 18).
Free domain for the first year: eligible TLDs and the domain renewal price.
Fair-use and backup policy pages must exist before the fair-use and backup lines render.
FTP accounts and domains per plan (ftpAccounts is null, not set; domains equals sites).
PHP workers: pmMaxChildren (20, 20, 40, 52) rests on estimates of PHP worker size. Check it against real server measurements before launch.
Extra Layer Security: describe what the add-on adds beyond the firewall, brute-force protection and malware scanning every plan includes. Its description must not render a placeholder.
Offsite backup prices: this file has 5 GB $3, 10 GB $5, 30 GB $9, 60 GB $13, 100 GB $25 and 250 GB $35; the Add-ons tab of the sheet has $2, $3, $7, $13, $20 and 200 GB at $35. Which is right?
First response: no plan has support.avgFirstResponse. At these prices each plan needs a stated first-response time.
Scale and WooCommerce: Scale's bestFor and description name WooCommerce stores while capabilities.wooCommerceOptimization is false.
Currencies: check the GBP, EUR, AED and INR prices before launch, and confirm that checkout (WHMCS) bills in the currency shown, with the same amounts.
